findings.scenario: A TypeScript class with constructor parameter properties (`export class A { constructor(public count: number, private readonly name: string) {} }`) now gets class-member Property ids `Property:a.ts:A.constructor.count@1:14` / `Property:a.ts:A.constructor.name@1:36` instead of `Property:a.ts:A.count` / `Property:a.ts:A.name`. These are public class members (HAS_PROPERTY from Class:A, ACCESSED cross-file from b.ts), not function-locals, so every stored reference, MCP uid, and diff/incremental consumer keyed on the old id breaks, and the qualified name wrongly claims the field belongs to `constructor`.
findings.evidence: Widening the prefix gate from callables to `isPositionQualifiedLocalLabel` (callable-labels.ts:42, adds Variable/Const/Property/Static) routes Property defs through `enclosingCallablePrefix`; for a parameter property the definition node sits inside the constructor's `method_definition` (a LOCAL_SCOPE_BODY type) below the `class_body` boundary, so the walk returns the constructor. Empirical probe with the diff compiled (runPipelineFromRepo, workerPoolSize 1): head => `Property:a.ts:A.constructor.count@1:14`, `HAS_PROPERTY Class:a.ts:A -> Property:a.ts:A.constructor.count@1:14`, `ACCESSES Function:b.ts:use -> Property:a.ts:A.constructor.count@1:14`; base dist => `Property:a.ts:A.count`. This contradicts the diff's own stated invariant in callable-labels.ts ('A class field stays unqualified even inside a function ... top-level and class-member ids are untouched'). The only new value-identity test (function-local-identity.test.ts) covers a plain function-local `const`, not class members.
findings.recommendation: Exclude class-member definitions from the value prefix: e.g. only apply the prefix to Property/Static when the def has no enclosing class owner (or treat `required_parameter`/`optional_parameter` with an accessibility modifier, and constructor bodies generally, as a prefix boundary for Property). Add a regression test asserting `Property:a.ts:A.count` for a TS parameter property alongside the existing local-value test.
